inShort: A feeds, and B drives with the elbows tucked to the hips, so the body does the work. Forehand first, then backhand.
rules: A feeds from across the net, out of the air or with a bounce. B stands 2–3 steps off the centre line.
B tucks the elbows against the hips and locks the arms to the body, like a T-Rex.
B hits from this position: the turn of the body moves the paddle, the arms just ride along. Keep your head still.
10 balls in pure T-Rex. Then let the arms go at contact and swing through.
tooEasy: Let the arms go at contact, and 3 of 5 balls have to land in one half. Even harder: hit standing on the left foot only.
tooHard: Stay in pure T-Rex, and the ball may go anywhere.
goodLooksLike: The ball still goes deep with the arms locked, and the head stays still through contact.
